title: Longitudinal models updated ICU mortality risk with incomplete records
summary: Longitudinal ICU models using MIMIC-III data predicted death 12–24 hours after an observation window. Multiple imputation expanded the analysis from 4,276 complete cases to 16,532 patients with 70 predictors while retaining similar discrimination; reported AUCs were about 0.78–0.79. The first public version with this result was the 2022-04-28 medRxiv preprint; the journal article followed in 2023. This retrospective proof of concept has no external validation or demonstrated clinical benefit.
ai_technology: Deep neural networks and penalized regression with multiple imputation

evidence.tested: Retrospective MIMIC-III analysis with repeated five-fold cross-validation; authors describe it as proof of concept and call for evaluation in other ICUs.
evidence.unknown: No independent, prospective or clinical-impact evaluation is reported unless specified in the tested field.
evidence.ai_role: Learned models updated short-term mortality estimates from longitudinal EHR measurements, and imputation addressed incomplete records.
